title: WPMS/2139/2018 of ARVIND KUMAR GUPTA Vs NAGAR PANCHAYAT LAKSAR THROUGH ITS EXECUTIVE OFFICER

paras.text:
WPMS No. 2139 of 2018
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
(Via Video Conferencing)
Mr. Siddhartha Singh, Advocate for the
petitioner.
Mr. R.C. Arya, Standing Counsel for
the State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. Parikshit Saini, Advocate for the
private respondents.
The brief facts of the case are the
respondent No.1, had initiated the proceedings
under Section 202 to be read with Rule 176
A(2) of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and
Land Reforms Act, and the Rules framed
thereunder; for the purposes of ejectment of
an Assami and for the determination of the
lease. The principal lessee or the Assami, in
question, had met with the sad demise on 17th
September, 2002. The petitioner had filed an
application before the Court of Assistant
Collector, 1st Class, in Case No. 1 of 2006-07,
Nagar Panchayat Vs. Mam Chand Gupta,
invoking the provisions contained under order
22 Rule 4 (3). In the said application thus
preferred on 5th March, 2008, he had prayed
for that in the absence of there being a
substitution made by the applicant to the
proceedings under Section 202 of the Act, the
proceedings may be abated.
Immediately after the filing of the said
application, the respondent No.1, herein, had
filed an application for impleadment on 20th
October, 2018. The argument of the learned
counsel for the petitioner is that this
application for impleadment, would not be
tenable in the proceedings under Section 202,
which are governed by the provisions of Z.A.
& L.R. Act, where the provisions of Section
341 of the Act provides, an applicability of the

procedure contemplated under the CPC, and
in that eventually, there could not have been
application for impleadment, rather it could be
an application for substitution of the heirs,
when the fact of the death of the father of the
petitioner was brought on record by his
application dated 5th March, 2008.
The second limb of argument of the
learned counsel for the petitioner is that the
application preferred by the respondent No.1
on 20th October, 2018, would not be tenable
for the reason that even if, it is presumed to be
an application under Order 22 Rule 3 and 4,
which would be applicable under Section 341
of the Act, it ought to have been accompanied
with the application for condonation of delay,
and also an application to set aside the
abatement for the reason being that the
proceedings otherwise automatically stood
abated in the absence of substitution being
made within the period of limitation provided
under Article 120.
This fact that the application preferred
by the respondent No.1 on 20th October, 2018,
to bring the son of late Mr. Mam Chand Gupta
did not accompany an application under
Section 5 of the Limitation Act, as well as
there was no application under Order 22 Rule
9, for setting aside abatement, the same could
not have been allowed by the Court of
Assistant Collector by the impugned order,
which is under challenge.
On this limited count itself because
otherwise also the law contemplates that in a
proceeding, which has been filed at a belated
stage, it must be accompanied with the
application for seeking condonation of delay
and it is only after the Condonation of delay,

that the Court gets assigned with its power to
deal with the application on its own merits.
In the absence of there being prayer for
condonation of delay, the application for
impleadment filed by respondent No. 1, even
if it is taken as to be an application under
Order 22 Rule 3 and 4, could not have been
allowed without condoning the delay and
without setting aside the abatement.
On that limited count itself, this Writ
Petition is allowed. The impugned order
dated 11th July, 2018, passed by the
Additional Collector in Revision No. 106 of
2011-12, Arvind Kumar Vs. Nagar Panchayat,
as well as order dated 25th November, 2008,
passed by the Assistant Collector in Case No.
1 of 2006-07, under Section 202 of the Act is
quashed. The Writ Petition is allowed.
However, allowing of this Writ Petition
will not prejudice the rights of the respondent
No.1 to file an appropriate application for
substitution of late Mr. Man Chand Gupta, as
permissible under law.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
Dated 18.08.2020
Shiv
